hausdorff_distance — 3D metrics op

• Data kinds: points × points → measurement

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.hausdorff_distance(a, b) (to call the implementation directly, import metrics3d; metrics3d.hausdorff_distance(a, b); from the registry, ops3d.get("hausdorff_distance"))

Usage

The symmetric Hausdorff distance = max(max_a min_b, max_b min_a). → scalar. The worst-case discrepancy.

Raises ValueError: if either is empty or not (N,3) (the maximum of an empty set would be a raw numpy exception).

Computation: with cKDTree, take the nearest-neighbour distances from each point of a to b and from b to a, and return the larger of the two directional maxima. It is the smallest radius guaranteeing "every point of one cloud lies within this distance of the other cloud". Unit = the coordinate unit.

Input: a, b are point clouds (N, 3) / (M, 3) (point counts may differ, no correspondence needed). Like its sibling chamfer_distance, it passes the input through _require_cloud at the entry: an empty point cloud or input that is not 3 columns, such as (N, 2), is rejected with a ValueError carrying this op's own message (previously an empty cloud made max() fail with numpy's "zero-size array", and input that is not 3 columns failed on cKDTree's dimension mismatch — neither says what is wrong).

Returns: Python float, [0, inf). 0 for identical point clouds. Not normalised.

Note: 1 outlier point determines the value (maximum, not mean). For evaluating noisy scans, chamfer_distance or fscore (fraction within the threshold tau) is more stable; use Hausdorff when you want to claim "at worst this accuracy" (tolerance verification, the same character as LOD max_error).
